subject: ProxyChain maintenance roll-forward and SLA credit modeling
body:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@proxychain.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: support@proxychain.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scheduled maintenance + overlapping probe windows

Hi Grace,

Quick heads up: we performed an emergency rolling maintenance on our egress cluster on 2026-08-14 between 22:40 and 23:25 PDT. We posted the notice in advance (attached maintenance_notice.pdf) but there was an unplanned extension for the final drain step. Some of your probes that run on 5-minute cadence saw elevated error rates and timeouts; we've attached our internal change log for the window.

We don't believe this constitutes a Redwood SLA credit trigger because the extension was due to a cascade from an upstream transit provider. That provider took a manual flap remediation and we were in the remediation chain. Happy to share logs and work with your team on how you want to account for the time.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Ops, ProxyChain, Inc.

---

From: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@proxychain.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scheduled maintenance + overlapping probe windows

Alex — thanks for the quick context and for attaching the notice. We pulled your maintenance_notice.pdf and our probe logs (attached as probe_logs.csv) and there are three things we need clarified before we close this out on the billing side:

1) Maintenance roll-forward semantics — our SLA calculation pipeline buckets availability into 1-minute resolution and then rolls windows to full-hour billing buckets. Because your drain extended 25 minutes past the scheduled end, some of our requests fell into the next hour bucket. We need to agree whether the maintenance should be rolled forward to the scheduled slot (i.e., treat the extension as still part of the original window) or whether it should be attributed to the later hour when the errors manifested. The choice materially changes the credit shown on our end.

2) Partial degradation handling — several of our calls saw high p50 latency but not full error rates for ~12 minutes. Do you treat that as full unavailability, or do you have a partial-degradation definition (percent of endpoints impacted over time) that we can use to apportion credits? Our model supports a time-weighted partial credit; we can provide the workbook with a suggested split.

3) Third-party cascade exception — you mentioned the upstream transit flap. Per our SLA, third-party outages that are not under ProxyChain control are eligible for exclusion only if they meet your published provider-exclusion criteria. Can you confirm the upstream postmortem link and the handoff timing so we can determine if an exclusion applies?

Ben — copying you for the suggested credit model; I sketched a proposal in sla_calc_workbook.xlsx that uses a roll-forward-to-scheduled-window assumption plus a 50/50 split for partial degradation minutes (time-weighted). Marissa — FYI since this affects the August billing cycle.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: probe_logs.csv, sla_calc_workbook.xlsx

---

From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@proxychain.com>, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scheduled maintenance + overlapping probe windows

Grace / Alex — I dug into the probe traces and the attached workbook. My notes:

- If ProxyChain is willing to apply a roll-forward (treat the extension as part of the scheduled maintenance window), the net visible SLA impact in our hourly buckets drops from 0.62% to 0.18% for the affected hour.
- For the ~12 minutes of elevated latency (p50 increased but p99 stayed below error threshold), our suggested approach is partial-crediting: allocate credit proportional to the fraction of failed endpoints *and* duration. In the workbook I used a conservative 50/50 split (half credit for those minutes) — happy to adjust if ProxyChain has a published policy.
- Regarding third-party exclusion: we need the exact timestamp when the upstream provider first reported the flap and when ProxyChain started active remediation. If ProxyChain's remediation began within the scheduled maintenance window and the cascade started during your scheduled change, that supports exclusion. If the transit flap occurred after your window or while you were already back to normal, we should not exclude it.

Action items:
- Alex: share upstream provider postmortem link + remediation timestamps (requesting those be added to support@proxychain.com thread).
- ProxyChain & Redwood to agree on roll-forward semantics for billing tables (either 'roll-to-original-window' or 'assign-by-observed-timestamp').
- We (Redwood) will accept partial-crediting methodology if ProxyChain publishes the criteria used in the workbook.

I'll draft the formal credit calculation once we have the provider timestamps; attaching a sample output table in the workbook.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Billing & Partner Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla_calc_workbook.xlsx

---

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@proxychain.com>
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, support@proxychain.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scheduled maintenance + overlapping probe windows

Ben / Grace — thanks for the concrete framing. We've just published a short postmortem on the upstream transit flap (https://status.proxychain.com/incidents/2026-08-transit-flap) and our internal remediation timestamp is 2026-08-14T23:10:00-07:00. The cascade that caused the extended drain clearly began during our scheduled window but the tail overlapped the next hour.

ProxyChain is willing to:
- Accept roll-forward to the original scheduled maintenance window for billing calculations (we will mark the extra 25 minutes as part of the scheduled event), and
- Approve a time-weighted partial-credit approach using the 50/50 multiplier Ben proposed for the latency-only minutes.

We'll prepare an official statement for your billing system and email it to support@proxychain.com; please confirm the final credit number on your side once you run the workbook with our timestamps.

Appreciate the collaborative approach here — I'll follow up with the postmortem PDF to the support thread.

—Alex
